priceSnapshot.note: BTC firmed overnight from the ~$64,300 endday mark to ~$65,250, a fresh ~5-week high that TAGGED the $65,406 rejection high (intraday $65,461) and pressed the ~$65,631 50-month EMA before easing back just under it. changePct +1.48% is computed session-over-session vs yesterday's $64,300 endday mark (both endpoints verified), not a clean exchange 24h figure. reduceIf.confirmation: A 4H close back below $63,000 loses the reclaimed floor and re-opens the $62,200 magnet — scale the remaining spot core down toward EXIT.

addIf.confirmation: A 1H/4H close above the ~$65,631 50-month EMA (not just a wick over $65,406) that HOLDS confirms a real breakout of the July range — only then redeploy raised cash into a momentum add. The $65,406 tag alone has already been rejected once, so the trigger is raised to a holding close above $65,631.

decisionBox.changed: Shift from HOLD to a small TAKE_PROFIT: BTC pushed into the $65,406/$65,631 double-rejection zone / 50-month EMA overnight, exactly the resistance the week has faded twice, and does so into the Jul 28-29 Fed meeting with the wallet holding only ~$6.6 cash (97% in the spot core). Rather than chase a top-of-range DCA (the week's own 'accumulate the floor, don't chase the top' lesson) or sit idle, trim a small ~15% slice of the spot core into the cap to rebuild dry powder for a post-Fed dip toward the $63,700 floor / $62,200 magnet. Keep 85% of the core for the breakout case; futures stay flat — no leverage into a binary Fed print. The add trigger is raised to a holding close above $65,631.

calibration.rollingRecord: The week's discipline is paying: accumulate spot at/above the floor, refuse leverage in a directionless tape, and now — with the core in modest profit and price at the cap — take a small profit into resistance rather than chase. Yesterday's range-bullish tilt (add $65,406) was right: price firmed from $64,300 to tag $65,461. The accumulated core (~0.00347 BTC, avg ~$63,990) is ~+2% as price pressed the cap; net worth ~$230, zero blow-ups.
